cells.tense: The closeness is here, real, and does not blur you into anyone else.
cells.ask: At the meal where it matters, say one thing you actually feel, not the version that keeps the peace. Then let the table carry it.
cells.core:
When you sit with people and something moves between you, you can let it land without losing yourself in it. Your own view of things stays with you. The warmth moves both ways and leaves room on both sides — which is why the people you share things with keep wanting to come back to it.

That is a strong position to stand in. What this balance is free to feed next is steadiness: staying near people while you keep your own footing. Not more feeling — holding what you already feel when it starts being asked to carry somebody else. The shape you have is rare, and it holds. Keep it near.
cells.sheetLine: You feel with people and stay yourself while you do it.
cells.verb: feeling with someone rather than only about them
cells.place: the shared meaning you keep handing down

cells.tense: You are already bracing for what someone will need next, before anyone has asked.
cells.ask: Let one thing that belongs to someone else stay with them today, even if you could hold it better. Let them finish it, or not.
cells.core:
You take on what people are carrying before they hand it to you. Their moods land in your body first. You can feel the argument about to happen, the grief under the bad week, and you are already arranging yourself around it. The one thing that has slipped is whose day you are standing in — yours or the room's.

That is the bend to notice. Wanting to help gets you there ahead of anyone asking. So let one thing that belongs to someone else stay with them today. You may have to sit through a discomfort you usually solve. What holds here is not less warmth. It is warmth that can tell whose it is.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what hasn't been handed to you yet.

cells.tense: The feelings went quiet at some point, and you have been keeping it that way.
cells.ask: Tell one person one true thing about how your week actually went, out loud, and let them hear it before you tidy it up.
cells.core:
The care you have for people stays out at arm's length. The conversations are fine; they just stay on the surface. The people around you may be getting your attention, your time, your competence — not a clear view of you. That's not coldness. It's a distance you keep, and it has held for a while.

What balance looks like here is an evenness that can hold something real without folding or shutting down. You don't have to feel more to get there. Pick one person and one thing you actually mean, and say it plainly. It doesn't have to be important. It just has to be true, in words they can hear.
cells.sheetLine: You keep care at arm's length, and it keeps out.

cells.tense: People come away from you feeling understood, and you call it just being practical.
cells.ask: Point at one small thing you did that changed the tone of someone's week, and call it what it was — your doing.
cells.core:
You are already doing the thing this describes. People bring you their hard news and leave steadier. They come back, they tell you things they don't tell others, and they feel met. It happens without you deciding to make it happen — in how you listen, what you ask, when you stay quiet. Your part in it doesn't feel like a part. It feels like the conversation went that way by itself.

The credit is what isn't landing. Seeing the shape of what you already do is what makes it something you can reach for on purpose, rather than something that only happens to you. The first person who needs to hear it is you.

attempts.check: The record gives the mechanism but no lived history, so any account of when the person went numb or what a room cost them would be invented; I keep the reference to the past vague and let them place it. A reader could reasonably say they are just reserved, or just practical, and not numb at all — so the reading points at distance people can feel and leaves it disownable. The asks survive being wrong: telling one story, naming one person, letting one thing end, all do something useful even if the read is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line claiming I know what they feel under the holding — I cut it; the card is theirs to confirm or refuse.
